title: Structured Log Harmonizer: session lineage + gap-healing for multi-source ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight harmonizer layer in the ingest pipeline that normalizes structured logs from polyglot producers, synthesizes deterministic session lineage when explicit correlation ids are missing, and performs gap-healing for short out-of-order bursts before writing to Loki/ELK backends. This reduces noise in downstream trace joins, improves dashboard fidelity for latency/error surfaces, and lowers reingest/backfill load.

Scope:
- Input sources: http/jsonl sidecars, kafka topics, edge-proxy forwards.
- Normalize to a compact canonical schema (timestamp_ns, tenant_id, service, span_id, parent_span_id, session_id, corr_id, level, message, structured_fields).
- Deterministic session lineage: derive session_id using stable hashing heuristics (client_ip/device_id/timestamp-window/service) when corr_id absent, with versioned provenance tag.
- Gap-healing: local buffer window (configurable up to 5s) to reorder and merge small out-of-order sequences and attach missing parent pointers where inferable.
- Emit enrichment tags to indicate synthesized fields and confidence score.
- Backward-compatible: do not drop original payload; preserve raw_json field for forensic replays.

Acceptance criteria:
1) <1% increase in ingest processing latency at 95p for steady-state traffic in staging (target: +<10ms).
2) Deterministic session_id generated for >=85% of messages that lack corr_id in synthetic workload.
3) Dashboard tests show 20% reduction in duplicate trace joins for services X/Y in canary.
4) Rollout with feature flag and tenant opt-out.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic synthesis vs best-effort probabilistic: we chose deterministic stable-hash heuristics to make later joins reproducible even if weakly unique, at cost of occasional collisions; collision risk mitigated by including provenance and confidence which downstream can use to filter.
- Local buffer window size: 0.5s default to keep latency low; provide tunable upper bound to 5s for bursty edge networks but gated by tenant SLOs.
- Enrichment vs mutation: add synthesized fields as annotated tags rather than replacing existing corr_id fields to preserve fidelity and auditability.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement harmonizer as a small processing stage in existing ingest proxy service (Go). Features: canonical mapper, deterministic session synthesizer, small ring buffer reorderer, synthesized metadata fields, metrics and trace hooks.
- Phase 2: add distributed coordination (optional) to share recent session fingerprints across instances for cross-shard inference if Phase 1 shows high collision rates.
- Phase 3: operator UI in Console to visualize synthesized sessions and tune buffer per-tenant.

Instrumentation and observability:
- Metrics: harmonizer.process_time_ns (summary), synthesized_session_rate, collision_rate_estimate, reordered_messages_total, dropped_after_window_total.
- Traces: add tracing hooks with a harmonizer span that records inference decisions and provenance tags.
- Dashboards: create a Canary dashboard showing before/after duplicate-join rate, session-coverage, and error-rate delta. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/harmonizer-canary (placeholder).
- Alerts: alert if collision_rate_estimate > 0.5% over 10m or if reordered_messages_total > expected baseline by 5x.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for mapping rules and hash stability.
- Integration tests with kafka fixtures and loki writer running in staging.
- Synthetic load test: replay of customer-traffic samples with missing corr_ids to validate session coverage and latency.
- Canary rollout: enable for internal tenants then opt-in list of pilot customers, monitor dashboards for 72h before wide release.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Structured+Log+Harmonizer
- Load test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-loadtests/pulls/217 (WIP)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/642 (draft)
- Example dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/harmonizer-canary

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: increased memory due to buffering under burst; Mitigation: hard limits per-tenant, backpressure to upstream and monitoring.
- Risk: false joins from weak fingerprints; Mitigation: provenance/confidence tags and canarying behind feature flag.
- Risk: operator confusion over synthesized fields; Mitigation: Console docs and an explicit opt-out tenant setting.

Next steps:
- Finish prototype PR and request internal code review (assigned to Marco).
- Run staging load tests and collect metrics.
- Prepare canary runbook and Console toggle.
